newsitem.title: DUBAI: Mideast Gulf oil outlook - tenders lead the way.
newsitem.headline: Mideast Gulf oil outlook - tenders lead the way.

text.p: Middle distillate sellers are betting on a series of buy tenders from the Indian subcontinent to turn around year-start price weakness, Gulf oil traders said on Thursday.
India, Sri Lanka and Nepal have lined themselves up to award a combined total of some 265,000 tonnes of gas oil, jet-kerosene and leaded gasoline over the next 10 days.
"The tenders will have to move the slack in the market...The Gulf is long in middle distillates and the arbitrage from the Mediterranean is narrowing but still open," said one trader.

India Oil Corp (IOC) held a major influence over short-term direction for Gulf prices and premiums, and could add to bearish Gulf sentiment by opting to take cargoes from the rival Mediterranean market, traders said.

IOC is in the market for 90,000 tonnes of gas oil for first-half February delivery, an attractive outlet for holders of Gulf cargoes who have faced subdued Asian demand and rising regional freight rates that have cut into Gulf competitiveness.
Bids submitted for Sri Lanka's gas oil, jet and leaded gasoline tenders were valid till January 9.
Gas oil was assessed at $29.85 a barrel fob Gulf on Thursday, a three percent loss since the year's start though its premium to independent price quotes held at 60-70 cents.
Jet-kerosene was valued at around $31.25 a barrel fob Gulf, adrift of the 1996 high of $33.55 hit in early December.

But large scale price falls were discounted by traders who highlighted cold weather in Europe and the absence of Iraqi refined products under the United Nations "oil-for-food" deal for the next six months as supportive.
"The Iraqis told us that they would not export products in the first six months," said one crude customer of Baghdad's State Oil Marketing Organisation (SOMO).
Iraq exported mainly gas oil and fuel oil before its 1990 invasion of Kuwait and traders believe Iraqi product flows will not resume till the end of the first quarter at the earliest.
